description: We are a team from Dushanbe, Tajikistan, taking part in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We love space, storytelling and web development. Our challenge is Abandoned but not Forgotten: we want to tell school-age space fans the stories of NASA hardware left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. We are looking for teammates who can draw, code or write in English.
summary:
Our project is an interactive educational website designed to introduce the modern generation to space, its exploration, and NASA's achievements. Our goal is to make science interesting and accessible, especially for young people.

The website features articles, stories, comics, and videos about legendary NASA robots, satellites, spacecraft, and telescopes. Users can explore the same topic in different formats: read articles, enjoy illustrated comics, or watch videos based on them. The platform also includes an interactive 3D Solar System model and educational games.

A special part of our project is Acustik, a fictional alien from another galaxy who guides users on their space journey.

Our mission is to combine education and entertainment, spark curiosity about science, and inspire the next generation to explore the universe!
details:
EXSPACE is an educational web platform that brings space missions to life through illustrated comics, companion stories, videos, games, and an animated AI guide named Akustik. Created for the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, it invites learners to discover the human stories and engineering achievements behind spacecraft, including explorers left on the Moon and Mars.

Our approach begins with curiosity. Instead of presenting mission information only as technical descriptions, EXSPACE offers several ways to explore it. The Missions library contains 58 collections, each with a comic and companion story. A built-in reader lets visitors turn pages, switch between formats, enlarge pages, and download the original PDFs. Search helps visitors find missions and destinations, while favorites let them save what interests them. The wider collection provides context beyond the challenge's focus on equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

The Videos section presents mission videos through embedded YouTube players, so visitors can watch them without leaving the platform. The Solar System section embeds NASA Eyes on the Solar System to connect individual missions with the worlds they explored. The Games section includes Space Flight and Akustik: The Way Home, a 3D adventure in which players explore Mars, encounter representations of NASA landers and rovers, find missing parts, and repair Akustik's ship.

Akustik gives the experience a memorable character. In our fictional story, he arrives on Earth from another universe, becomes separated from his family, and joins EXSPACE while searching for a way home. His experience connects emotionally with the project's theme of distant explorers and spacecraft left behind. As a 2D animated AI companion powered by Gemini, he answers questions about space, helps visitors navigate the platform, and suggests comics or videos related to their interests. His fictional biography is separate from real mission history and established astronomy.

We built the platform with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and a Python backend. SQLite stores optional accounts, favorites, and quiz results. Three.js supports the 3D game. NASA mission pages, historical references, and imagery provide source material; photo credits are recorded in the repository. AI requests pass through the backend so API credentials are kept out of the public website and repository.

The project is designed for students, families, and curious newcomers. Its intended impact is to make space history approachable, encourage further exploration of NASA resources, and help visitors appreciate the lasting scientific and cultural value of missions beyond their active lifetimes. We considered different learning preferences, mobile layouts, reduced-motion settings for the companion, and guest access to the main educational content. These are design goals and implemented features, not claims of measured learning outcomes.

The full source code and project media are available in our public GitHub repository, with instructions for running the platform locally and deploying its backend.

CONFIRMED AI-USE DESCRIPTION

AI tools were used in several parts of EXSPACE. Devin assisted in creating the comics, videos, and 3D game models. ChatGPT assisted in creating the 2D Akustik mascot and his fictional character narrative. ChatGPT/Codex also supported software implementation and iteration. The Gemini API powers Akustik's conversational responses. NASA source photographs and mission references are distinct from our AI-assisted creative content and fictional storytelling.

For the SI-use selection, choose the available options corresponding to code generation, text generation, image/art generation, video generation, 3D asset generation, and an AI chatbot. Use the exact choices offered by the form. Before submitting, ensure AI-generated images and videos carry the visible labels required by the submission form; this disclosure alone does not replace those labels.
